skill.name: creating-commands
skill.description: Create and review Claude Code slash commands using templates, naming rules, argument guidance, frontmatter options, and validation checklists.
skill.summary: Guides creation and review of Claude Code slash commands with templates and best practices.
skill.author: BrendanShields

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown examples, inline code, and documented Claude Code command locations. I found no evidence of prompt injection, data exfiltration, or malicious intent. One medium-risk content issue remains because examples normalize broad Bash allowlists for generated commands.

remediation.issue: Broad Bash permissions in command examples
remediation.suggestion: Replace Bash(bash:*) examples with narrow allowlists that match each command, such as Bash(npm:*) only when npm is required.

remediation.issue: Personal command directory can persist behavior across projects
remediation.suggestion: Ask for explicit confirmation before writing under ~/.claude/commands/ and prefer project commands when sharing with a team.

static_findings.snippet: | `$ARGUMENTS` | All arguments as one string | `/cmd foo bar` → `foo bar` |
| `description` | Shown in help, enables auto-invoke | Recommended |
| `allowed-tools` | Tools the command can use | If using tools |
| `argument-hint` | Documents expected args | If has args |

semantic_findings.title: Overly Broad Generated Tool Permissions
semantic_findings.description: The command format examples include broad Bash permissions such as Bash(bash:*). Generated slash commands with broad Bash permissions can run arbitrary shell commands when invoked, so authors should prefer narrow allowlists.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The lines are examples, not active execution, but users may copy them into generated commands. This creates a realistic permission-scoping risk without evidence of malicious intent.

content.value_statement: Developers need dependable Claude Code slash commands that follow consistent structure and tool boundaries. This skill guides requirement gathering, template selection, and validation for reusable command files.
actual_capabilities: Collects command purpose, argument needs, and scope before generating a command.
Selects basic, argument-based, or workflow templates for different command types.
Documents naming rules, command locations, frontmatter fields, and argument syntax.
Provides examples for tests, linting, issue fixes, code review, and deployment workflows.
Reviews existing commands against documented anti-patterns and validation checklists.
limitations: It does not execute generated commands or verify runtime behavior.
It assumes Claude Code slash command conventions.
Commands with Bash permissions still require human review before use.
Personal command installation may modify files under the user's Claude configuration directory.

use_cases.title: Create a Project Command
use_cases.description: Generate a team-visible slash command with clear purpose, scope, frontmatter, and validation steps.

use_cases.title: Standardize Command Templates
use_cases.description: Define repeatable command structures for testing, reviews, issue fixes, and workflow automation.

use_cases.title: Review Existing Commands
use_cases.description: Check command names, arguments, tool permissions, and prompts against documented best practices.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Command
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a command without arguments.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a simple Claude Code slash command named [name]. It should [purpose]. It does not need arguments. Use project scope.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Command With Arguments
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for user input handling.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Claude Code slash command named [name] that accepts [arguments]. Include an argument hint and clear validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Workflow Command
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request using skills, agents, or tool permissions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a workflow command for [goal]. It may use [skill or agent]. Define the narrowest required tools and expected output.

prompt_templates.title: Audit and Improve a Command
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of an existing command file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Claude Code command for naming, frontmatter, arguments, tool permissions, and prompt clarity. Suggest concrete fixes.

output_examples.input: Create a lint-check command for a JavaScript project.
output_examples.output: A project scoped slash command named lint-check with a concise description, npm lint permission, step-by-step instructions, and validation notes.

output_examples.input: Review an existing command that fixes GitHub issues.
output: Findings grouped by naming, frontmatter, arguments, and tool permissions.
Specific changes that improve clarity, safety, and command reuse.

output_examples.input: Create a deployment workflow command for staging.
output_examples.output: A deployment command plan that runs tests, builds artifacts, performs pre-deploy checks, deploys to staging, and reports verification results.

best_practices: Choose the narrowest tool permissions that support the command.
Document expected arguments with clear hints and examples.
Validate generated commands against naming, frontmatter, and prompt checklist items.
anti_patterns: Do not use broad Bash permissions when a narrower allowlist works.
Do not hardcode local paths or environment-specific values.
Do not create vague commands without clear purpose, inputs, and success criteria.

faq.question: What kind of commands does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates Claude Code slash commands for development tasks, workflow steps, and reusable project automation.

faq.question: Can it create commands with arguments?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports all arguments, positional arguments, and file references used by Claude Code commands.

faq.question: Does it run the generated command?
faq.answer: No. It creates or reviews command content, but runtime behavior still needs user verification.

faq.question: Where are commands saved?
faq.answer: The skill documents project commands under .claude/commands/ and personal commands under ~/.claude/commands/.

faq.question: Can it help with command security?
faq.answer: It encourages explicit tool permissions, clear prompts, argument hints, and review against known anti-patterns.

faq.question: Is it useful outside Claude Code?
faq.answer: The guidance is specific to Claude Code, but the planning approach can inform similar AI command workflows.
